name: budget-tracker-tui
description: A TUI budget tracker app built in rust. Designed to track income and expenses and help visualize and gather basic insights from your transactions.
readme_summary: Budget Tracker TUI is a terminal-based application built with Rust that allows users to track personal income and expenses. It provides features for managing transactions, visualizing financial data through charts and summaries, and setting budgets.
key_features: Add, edit, delete, filter, and sort income and expense transactions
Hierarchical categories and subcategories with fuzzy search
Monthly and category summaries with interactive charts
primary_use_case: Tracking personal finances and gaining insights into spending habits through a terminal interface.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old owl perched on a stack of glowing coins, meticulously sorting and organizing them into different labeled jars representing income, expenses, and savings. The owl uses its keen eyes to analyze charts and graphs that float in the air around it, displaying financial trends. Subtle digital particles and faint code snippets emanate from the jars, hinting at the app's functionality. The background is a cozy, dimly lit study, with a small, stylized terminal window showing the 'Budget Tracker TUI' logo. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a warm, inviting color palette and clear, defined elements.

name: GPU-Share
description: GPUMesh lets people you trust run Docker GPU jobs on your machine — and lets you run jobs on theirs — over authenticated peer-to-peer connections. No SSH, no VPN, no cloud that sees your workload. Pair once, allowlist stays default-deny, jobs stay in containers.
readme_summary: GPUMesh enables secure, peer-to-peer sharing of Docker GPU jobs among trusted users without relying on centralized cloud services or complex network configurations like SSH or VPNs. It facilitates turning idle NVIDIA GPUs into a private, distributed compute network.
key_features: Authenticated peer-to-peer connections for Docker GPU jobs
No SSH, VPN, or cloud infrastructure required
QUIC P2P networking with optional relay
Docker + NVIDIA job execution with VRAM hints and retries
Group management for teams of GPUs
File copy and sandboxed command execution
Local dashboard for monitoring and control
primary_use_case: To create a private, secure, and distributed network for running Dockerized GPU workloads among trusted peers, leveraging idle GPU resources without external cloud dependencies.
cover_image_prompt: A vibrant, stylized illustration of a network of interconnected computers, each represented by a glowing NVIDIA GPU icon. These GPUs are linked by luminous data streams, forming a secure, private cloud-like structure in a digital space. One computer is actively sending a Docker container icon through the network, which is then received and processed by another GPU icon. Subtle UI elements showing job progress and container status are visible on small, floating screens. The overall mood is secure and collaborative, with a clean, modern aesthetic and a color palette of blues, greens, and oranges, rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style.

name: tuitter
readme_summary: tuitter is a terminal UI client for X (Twitter) built with TypeScript and OpenTUI. It allows users to authenticate with their X account and interact with content directly from their terminal.
key_features: Optional screen-time limit with daily tracking
primary_use_case: Interacting with X (Twitter) content directly from the command line interface.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, retro computer terminal screen displaying a vibrant, simplified feed of X (Twitter) posts. A user's hand, holding a glowing cursor, is shown interacting with the feed, highlighting posts and composing new ones. Subtle digital particles flow from the terminal, representing data streams. The repository name 'tuitter' is subtly integrated into the terminal's design. The overall scene is set in a dimly lit, cozy room, emphasizing focused interaction. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a color palette of blues, purples, and whites, conveying a sense of efficient and accessible social media engagement within a terminal environment.

name: caesium-app-web
description: A modern, privacy aware web app to compress images, all offline and within the browser.
readme_summary: Caesium Web Image Compressor is a privacy-focused, offline web application that allows users to compress JPG, PNG, and WebP images directly in their browser. It supports both lossy and lossless compression, preserves image metadata, and offers a before/after comparison feature, ensuring no images are uploaded or processed on external servers.
key_features: Runs entirely on your browser, no images are uploaded or processed on any external server
primary_use_case: Compressing images offline and in-browser for privacy and efficiency.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, stylized robot hand gently holding a large, uncompressed image file (represented as a detailed, high-resolution photo). The robot's other hand is holding a much smaller, compressed version of the same image, glowing with efficiency. The transformation is visualized by a subtle stream of digital particles flowing from the large image to the small one, indicating data reduction without loss of quality. The background is a clean, minimalist browser window interface, with the 'Caesium' logo subtly integrated into a corner. The overall mood is bright and secure, emphasizing privacy and ease of use. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with soft lighting and a clean, modern aesthetic.
